title: Landau damping and mode-selective instability of a vortex gas
authors: H. Terças, J. L. Figueiredo, J. T, Mendonça
abstract: We show that a collisionless point-vortex gas behaves as a genuine Vlasov system. Starting from the non-canonical Hamiltonian structure of point-vortex dynamics, we derive a reduced Klimontovich equation and the corresponding Vlasov description directly on the physical plane, without introducing auxiliary momentum variables. The theory predicts a rich spectrum of collective phenomena, including vortex Rossby-like waves, global oscillations, resonant critical layers, and a dielectric response operator analogous to that of plasmas and self-gravitating systems. For smooth vortex distributions, differential rotation gives rise to a vortex analogue of Landau damping, whereby collective modes transfer energy and angular momentum to resonant vortex annuli in the absence of collisions or dissipation. Remarkably, differential rotation acts as a stringent mode-selection mechanism: for a Gaussian vortex cloud, only a single quadrupolar quasi-mode survives, while all higher multipoles are destroyed by phase mixing. We further predict a vortex counterpart of the beam--plasma instability, in which a thin vortex ring orbiting an Onsager patch selectively excites Kelvin modes with an azimuthal symmetry controlled by the ring population. These results establish kinetic theory as a natural framework for collective vortex dynamics and suggest new mechanisms for vortex transport, vortex avalanches, and rotational glitches in neutron-star superfluids.
summary: This paper develops a kinetic theory for a collisionless gas of point vortices, showing that their collective behavior mirrors that of plasmas. Key findings include the prediction of vortex Landau damping and a strong mode-selection mechanism that filters out higher multipoles. This establishes kinetic theory as a natural framework for understanding vortex transport in astrophysical superfluids.
main_problem: To establish a systematic kinetic theory for collective vortex dynamics in a collisionless point-vortex gas, connecting microscopic dynamics to macroscopic collective behavior.
main_result: The theory predicts phenomena analogous to plasma physics, including Landau damping and a mode-selection mechanism where differential rotation selectively excites only the quadrupolar quasi-mode for a Gaussian cloud.
method: The authors derive a reduced Klimontovich equation and utilize the Vlasov formalism adapted for the non-canonical Hamiltonian structure of vortex interactions.
model_or_system: The system is a gas of point vortices interacting via long-range logarithmic potentials in two dimensions. The dynamics are governed by a non-canonical Poisson bracket, leading to a Vlasov-like kinetic equation.
key_observables: Vortex Rossby-like waves, global oscillations, the dielectric response operator, and the damping rate of the quadrupolar quasi-mode.
important_parameters: The collisionless limit ($	au_{coll} \gg t_{dyn}$), the vortex density ($N_v$), and the azimuthal number ($m$).
main_assumptions: The system is treated as an incompressible, 2D gas, and the analysis focuses on the collisionless regime, neglecting explicit pinning or mutual friction.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate normal modes for a cold vortex gas in a circular patch, showing spatial configurations and normalized Fourier transforms of moments for different multipoles.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the kinetic theory, moving from the full continuity equation to the Vlasov limit, analyzing the dispersion relation using WKB approximations, and finally deriving the mode selection rules via the dielectric response operator.
why_interesting: The work provides a powerful analogy between vortex dynamics (relevant in superfluids like neutron stars) and established plasma physics, utilizing kinetic theory methods applicable to complex many-body systems.
